seed_note:
Both seeds score 0.9601 on refined gold. That is not a duplicate: the two models have different parameter sums, their logits differ by up to 1.48, and they disagree on 10 of 376 predictions -- the disagreements happen to cancel. Two independently seeded models landing on the same number is stronger evidence than one model landing on it.

WHAT THIS MODEL IS. A binary triage gate over the complexity signal: TRIVIAL (the 4-tier taxonomy's SIMPLE) versus WORK (MEDIUM, COMPLEX and REASONING). It answers 'can a tiny model or a cache serve this, or does it need the main model?'

HOW THIS FOLD WAS CHOSEN, AND WHY THAT MATTERS. The other complexity gates in this family were picked by hand -- one because the deployed Praxis table routes that way, one because it was the obvious binary. Neither was chosen by measurement. Enumerating EVERY contiguous fold of the 4-tier ladder and ranking by three-juror agreement found this one instead:
    SIMPLE | MEDIUM+COMPLEX+REASONING   86.9% agreement, 19.0% minority
    SIMPLE+MEDIUM | COMPLEX+REASONING   82.0% agreement, 24.6% minority  (the route gate)
It scores 0.9601 against the route gate's 0.9269 median at an almost identical majority baseline (80.32% vs 80.59%), so the comparison is like-for-like: +3.32 points for choosing the split by measurement rather than by intuition.

READ THE BASELINE. Majority baseline is 80.32%; 96.01% clears it by 15.7 points, and TRIVIAL recall is 94.59% on a class that is 19.7% of the eval, so the minority class is doing real work. TRIVIAL precision is 86.42% -- about 5% of WORK prompts get sent down the cheap path, which is the error direction to watch if the cheap path is much weaker.

WEAKEST POINT, STATED. On the 176 rows where the three-model jury SPLIT, this model scores 80.11% against an 82.95% majority baseline -- below it -- and TRIVIAL recall falls to 43.33%. Contested rows are roughly 30% of real traffic for this signal. On the rows the jury agreed on, jury agreement is 100% by construction and the model gets 96.01%.
